I think one of the main purposes of the /v/freeculture subverse has to be to discuss and explain free culture and free culture licenses. Why are non-commercial licenses and no-derivatives licenses non-free? And what are the advantages of using public domain or CC0 over using free licenses.

I think another purpose needs to be to find and share media that is legally available for reuse under free software licenses.

But in order to be good advocates for free culture I think we also have to be accepting of people who have not yet drank the water. That is, they don't get it. Most people don't really get the distinction between free as in libre or free as in beer. And I myself may occasionally post links to free as in beer media just because it's good and worth the time.

Still links like the Nina Paley above need to remain the center of our focus. I want some stuff I can use!

I like looking at watches, especially nifty designs. I get a little weary of watch memes like Seiko 5s and NATO straps. I prefer my Citizen CB0020-50E over just about any watch I see because I like the solar power and atomic time sync feature. While I think a lot of mechanicals look awesome, I can't get over the idea of them being less accurate than quartz watches. My ideal watch would be a quartz movement, with solar power, atomic time sync, tritium tubes (like a luminox), and a sweeping hand like a mechanical. I know quarts watches with sweeps exist (maybe even with solar), but I haven't seen one with time sync.

Before I had a watch that syncs the time, I was the kinda dude that would frequently check my time against another source for accuracy. Now, I check other sources against my watch to determine their accuracy. As an IT guy this is pretty helpful when working on servers.
